name: Hardware upgrade add-on
definition: Unit that plugs into a console to add processors, graphics or memory hardware so that it runs games made for the upgraded system (32X type).
notes: Sega 32X plugs into Genesis, adds two SH-2 processors and RAM, own cartridge library.

name: Network or modem adapter made for one console
definition: Adapter that adds a dial-up modem, broadband or wireless network connection to one console through its own port or bay; a standard USB network adapter is D1.
notes: GameCube Broadband Adaptor and Modem Adaptor listed, hardware class Network Interface; Sega Mega Modem, NetLink listed.

name: Game microphone
definition: Microphone made and sold to plug into a console as game input, for singing or voice commands (SingStar type); a headset is D3 and a speech microphone sold for computers is D1.
notes: SingStar Microphones sold as accessory pair with USB dongle; N64 Mic NUS-021 also listed.

name: Media add-on made for one console
definition: Remote control, playback kit or TV tuner made to add disc, video or TV functions to one console.
notes: Xbox One Media Remote 1577 and Digital TV Tuner 1611; 360 Media Remote and Universal Media Remote.

name: Console mouse
definition: Mouse or trackball made to plug into one console as pointing input; a mouse with a standard connector sold for computers is D1.
notes: Super NES Mouse listed as two-button mouse for compatible games on SNES.

name: Keyboard made for one console
definition: Keyboard made to plug into one console for typing, programming or text entry in games; a keyboard with a standard connector is D1.
notes: Family BASIC Keyboard HVC-007 on Famicom expansion port; XBAND Keyboard for SNES listed.

name: Paddle or spinner controller
definition: Controller with a rotary knob whose turn sets a position on screen (paddle, spinner, Vaus type).
notes: Atari CX-30 paddle controllers sold as twin pair; Arkanoid Vaus knob-and-potentiometer controller documented.

name: Phone VR viewer
definition: Headset that encloses the eyes and holds a phone as its display and compute (Cardboard, Gear VR type).
notes: Google Cardboard, Daydream View and Samsung Gear VR listed as phone-based viewers.

name: Rumble pack
definition: Add-on that plugs into one console's controller to make it vibrate (Rumble Pak, Jump Pack, Vibration Pack).
notes: Rumble Pak plugs into N64 controller; DS version and third-party Tremor Pak, Nyko Hyper Pak Plus.

name: Arcade system board
definition: Circuit board, with its game ROMs, cartridge or disc slot, that runs games inside a coin-operated video cabinet (JAMMA, Naomi, Atomiswave, MVS type).
notes: Sega Naomi motherboard sold in arcade-board shop category; Wikipedia lists Sega arcade system boards.
